mcp_operation_unsupported.description: actinglab-mcp lists this tool, the tool of an operation table row, but this build serves no call of it: the call was refused before anything was sent, run or written; mcp_tool names the tool.
mcp_operation_unsupported.common_causes: A call of a tool whose row this build does not serve yet: since Workflow #434 LAB-5G2b it serves the rows actinglab's CLI module serves and, on Windows, the rescue rows the rescue module serves, and refuses the three app rows and standard-pack check, the debugging and authoring rows actinglab's own commands serve and record draft, which the later slices of LAB-5 serve; and deploy and rollback, which through MCP run detached: the module's detached run is an actinglab.exe handed the initiator in ACTINGCOMMAND_INITIATOR, which refuses Lab-MCP, so the operation would answer detached and never run, until a detached run carries Lab-MCP (with LAB-6).
mcp_operation_unsupported.handling: Run the operation with actinglab (actinglab --json and the row's words), or through actingctl mcp-serve, until a build of actinglab-mcp that serves the tool is installed; sending the same call again answers the same.

mcp_identity_declaration_refused.description: The Runtime refused the governance identity card actinglab-mcp declares before a write (client actingctl-mcp, Workflow #434 LAB-5G2b, until LAB-6 removes the step); the write went ahead without it, and the Runtime's refusal is the caused_by link. It stands where actingctl mcp-serve answers mcp_identity_card_refused with mcp_blocker.
mcp_identity_declaration_refused.common_causes: actingd's governance.allowed_clients does not admit actingctl-mcp, so the Runtime refused the card as a client not allowed (governance_client_not_allowed) and recorded its own warning event; it still takes the write from the (Cli, Cli) envelope.
mcp_identity_declaration_refused.handling: Nothing is lost: the client action and the write were recorded and sent, and the answer is the write's. To stop the warning, the person adds actingctl-mcp to governance.allowed_clients in actingd.config.json, which actingd reads at its start.

mcp_job_started.description: actinglab-mcp serves the call as a job (Workflow #434 LAB-5G3), and the job goes on: the line's handle names it and job_phase says where it is (running, or submitting for a run). It answers a call not done within the server's call budget, ac_run_start at once (its handle is the run's Runtime request id) and ac_run_show of a job that still runs.
mcp_job_started.common_causes: The operation takes longer than the call budget (the start option --call-budget, 25 seconds by default): a drain, an emulator control, a stop and reset, a wait, a large read; or the call was ac_run_start, which answers before the run's receipt.
mcp_job_started.handling: Follow the handle with ac_run_show (id the handle, wait_s up to the call budget) until it answers the job's line; do not send the call again. A handle other than a run's lives only as long as this server process (then handle_unknown); a run's is read from the Runtime by any process.
